American Express · The Relationship Platform · 2020 to 2025

Where a Small Business goes daily to manage their Cash Flow

A primacy platform, and a net-new revenue engine

American Express set out to win the primary financial relationship with Small Business. In four years, these are the numbers that moved.

How it got there: one goal, and five big moves.

The background

A payments network that runs on transactions

American Express is a global, closed-loop payments network and card issuer. It earns through fees and interest on a high-volume, high-frequency transaction model. Every point of growth depends on acquiring, underwriting, servicing and engaging tens of millions of Card Members at scale.

US$72.2Brevenue, net of interest expense, FY2025
US$1.67Tbilled business worldwide, FY2025
86.6Mproprietary cards in force
~76,800colleagues worldwide
41%of worldwide billed business from Small Business and corporate clients

So what US Small Business Credit Card Market Share. Yet American Express did not hold the primary relationship. The Card was in the wallet, but the business's money, and the daily decisions about it, sat somewhere else.

Sources: American Express 2025 Form 10-K; Q4 2025 earnings release and presentation. Small and mid-sized businesses are those with annual revenue under US$300M.

The goal

Win the primary financial relationship

86% of US Small Business Customers are looking for an all in one Cash Flow Management Tool.

The customer need
  • See all money in and money out, in one place
  • Hold enough working capital to run today and grow tomorrow
  • Feel confident the next decision is a good one
  • Feel known and secure, with a provider they trust
  • Respect for their time: easy and simple to use
The goal

Become the place a Small Business manages its money

The first thing an owner checks every morning.

Leading indicators to primacy
  • Application conversion
  • Time to first, then second product
  • Monthly Active Transacting Users
  • Customer satisfaction

Primacy is products per customer times transactions. A Card alone could not move either far enough.

So what

American Express could not get there on its own. It needed the infrastructure, a forcing mechanism inside the business and an operating model built for speed. So in 2020 it bought Kabbage Lending, Amex’s biggest acquisition.

How it won

Five big moves

Each one on its own was a project. Together they changed what American Express was to a Small Business.

  1. 1

    Reorganised by customer segments and one relationship platform

    Product silos replaced by capability hubs, built once for every product and held together by reciprocal scorecards.

    →
  2. 2

    Redesigned the full experience around needs and actions

    Digital and human, end to end, organised around what a customer came to do rather than which product they held.

    →
  3. 3

    Made Cash Flow a service, and a growth driver

    Every internal and external account in one view, forecast ahead, powering the experience, marketing, credit and growth.

    →
  4. 4

    A single application experience for all products

    Answer once, one question per page, dynamic depending on product intent and existing customer data.

    →
  5. 5

    Worked differently

    Startup principles, sharper planning and prioritisation, flexible capacity and faster release cycles.

    →

Move 1 · Structure

Organised by customer segment, not by product

Two restructures. First, Global Commercial Services moved from product verticals to customer segments. Then, inside Small Business, one relationship platform took ownership of everything every product shared.

Reciprocal scorecards. Neither side could hit its number by ignoring the other, so the model held through growth and revenue pressure.

Move 2 · Experience

Redesigned end to end around what customers came to do

Product menus gave way to quick actions. Every account, at American Express or another bank, sat in one view with cash flow first. The human side moved with it: frontline and back office worked from one servicing platform.

Move 3 · Cash flow as a service

Cash flow, not cards, at the centre

A business runs on cash flow across every account it holds, including accounts at other banks. Bringing all of it into one data set, and forecasting ahead, gave owners a reason to come back daily. It also gave credit, marketing and product one shared picture of the customer.

The cash flow data layer Every internal and external account, in one data set

Experience

  • A dashboard and navigation that changed with the relationship
  • Cash flow insights and in-product cross-sell
  • Servicing context and cost to serve

Credit and risk

  • Underwriting and limit assignment
  • Real-time exposure across the relationship
  • Portfolio monitoring and capital allocation

Growth

  • Marketing eligibility and pre-approval
  • Propensity and next best action models
  • Sales prioritisation and routing
97% to 98%accuracy forecasting 90 days of working capital
2×engagement for customers with connected external accounts
9% to 12%insight-driven cross-sell conversion, A/B tested against a held-out control

Move 4 · One application

One seamless application for every product

Every product had its own application, rules and pend process. The business went after all of them at once: one application across Lending, Checking and Payments, with the rules behind it streamlined.

Answer once

Any starting product, the same application

One question per page, pre-filled from the Card account, with click-through tracked at every step. A second product asked only the incremental questions, and took about two minutes.

Walk through the application →
9 to 6 minapplication time
82% to 97%application click-through
60% to 81%straight-through processing
40% to 28%pend rate

Move 5 · Ways of working

A startup inside a regulated Fortune 100

A new structure does not make anyone faster on its own. The team also changed how it planned, chose what to build and shipped.

Startup principles

Systems before headcount

Build and show, rather than propose and wait. Minimum viable structure. Reuse and modularity as a team belief.

Planning and prioritisation

Ready, highest-value work first

Outcomes reviewed quarterly, leading indicators weekly, and guardrails so no win broke something else.

Flexible capacity~60%of engineering fungible

Across Lending, Payments and Platform. Run-the-business capacity fixed and cut every year.

Velocity10 to 2weeks per release cycle

Five releases in the time it used to take to ship one. +25% delivery velocity.

What the market saw

Launched to national coverage

In January 2023 the platform launched publicly as American Express Business Blueprint, and the Kabbage brand was retired.
